doc.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012

title: What he listens to now
summary: He listens to Pandora, Karl Berger, Howard Johnson's Gravity and Mingus Plays Mingus.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Well that was a question I should have prepared you for. What do you listen to these days as far as jazz?

You know I listen to Pandora. I don’t go too much out of my way to sit down and listen, though I have it on. Sometimes Pandora and I have it tuned to Clifford Brown and also to bebop, stuff comes up. I just got another car with a great stereo system and I listened to two records that just kill me. A little known album by Karl Berger, done in the early nineties. It’s a semi-big-band with Enrico Rava and all sorts of people and with Ingrid Sertso singing called “No Man is an Island.” I could listen to that forever. It’s an incredible recording. And then I also have Howard Johnson’s “Gravity.” Do you know the Gravity band?

That band was four years in the making. He kept on trying to put it together and I think he released that in the mid-nineties also. It’s a great album. Unbelievable solos. So that’s two pieces. Let’s see what else. I’ve got a wonderful CD, “Mingus Plays Mingus.” It’s Mingus playing the piano. Do you know that CD? I love that CD. And this is like something else, what do I listen to. The minute you walk out of here I’ll tell you everything else I listen to.
